No originalData/data modeling existed at all -- it fell into the generic ExtensionNode fallback, and InlineElement.data_ref merely read attribute values without resolving them to anything.

inputs.acceptance_evidence: 10 new tests prove: originalData round-trips through dumps/reload, structural ordering (before segments), dataRef/dataRefStart/dataRefEnd resolution (positive and negative), pc pairing enforcement (both one-sided-missing directions), and source/target independence.

execution_steps: 1. Read the pinned XLIFF 2.1 spec HTML directly (.local/format-contracts/acquired/xliff/src-xliff-001.bin) for originalData's (4.2.2.10) and data's (4.2.2.11) formal content models: originalData is a unit-level container of one-or-more data elements; data holds non-translatable text plus zero-or-more cp elements, with a REQUIRED id attribute.

2. Confirmed via reading reader.py's _parse_unit dispatch loop that <originalData> currently fell into the generic 'else: unit.children.append(_extension(child))' branch -- preserved as an opaque byte blob, not typed or validated, but also not silently lost (an existing preservation safety net).

3. Read the pinned XLIFF 2.1 schematron directly (.local/format-contracts/acquired/xliff/src-xlf-002.bin, schemas/xliff_core_2.1.sch) for the exact dataRef-family resolution rules: F15 (generic dataRef on any inline element must resolve to a data id in the same unit), F16S/F16T (pc's dataRefEnd must resolve, source/target separately), F17S/F17T (pc's dataRefStart must resolve, source/target separately), plus each pattern's second assertion requiring dataRefStart/dataRefEnd to be used as a pair.

4. Added DataElement(id, content: list[InlineNode], dir, attributes) to model/document.py, reusing InlineNode for data's content since its content model (text + optional cp children) is structurally identical to source/target's mixed content -- a cp child simply round-trips generically as InlineElement, matching this package's existing precedent for unmodeled tags rather than inventing dedicated cp modeling. Added Unit.original_data: list[DataElement].

5. Wired reader.py's _parse_unit to recognize <originalData> and parse it via a new _parse_original_data() into the typed field, reusing the existing generic _parse_inline() for each <data>'s content.

6. Wired writer.py's _write_unit to call a new _write_original_data(), emitting the container in the correct position (immediately after notes, before segments, matching the unit content model's own declared order) -- reusing the existing generic _serialize_inline() for each <data>'s content.

7. Verified model+reader+writer round-trip interactively before touching the validator: parsed a 2-data-element fixture, confirmed typed content, re-serialized, confirmed byte-level structural correctness and reload fidelity -- correct on the first attempt.

8. Added _data_ref_diagnostics(unit, diagnostics) to validator.py: resolves every dataRef/dataRefStart/dataRefEnd attribute on any inline element against the unit's original_data ids (checked per content type, source/target independently), and flags a pc with only one of dataRefStart/dataRefEnd present as unpaired.

9. Verified interactively before writing formal tests: resolved dataRef valid; unresolved dataRef a violation; paired dataRefStart/dataRefEnd both resolved valid; start-only unpaired; end-unresolved-with-start-present a violation; no dataRef usage anywhere stays clean -- all 6 cases correct on the first attempt.

10. Ran the full pre-existing xliff suite (397 tests, zero new fixtures) against the new check BEFORE writing any new test -- surfaced ONE genuine, pre-existing false positive: test_production_namespace.py's SAMPLE constant had a <pc dataRefStart="d1" dataRefEnd="d2"> with no <originalData> anywhere in the document at all, meaning this fixture was never actually spec-conformant (the ids never resolved to anything real). Fixed by adding a matching <originalData> block with real <data id="d1">/<data id="d2"> elements to the fixture -- the same 'correct the fixture, not the validation' discipline already applied this session (XLIFF Event 206, UBL Event 191) -- re-ran and confirmed all 397 pre-existing tests pass with the corrected fixture.
11. Wrote 10 formal tests, all passing on the first attempt.

12. Ran ruff (clean across all 8 changed files), the full xliff suite (407 passed, was 397, +10), and the full 6-format regression (3314 passed, was 3304, +10; same 4 pre-existing unrelated safetensors interop failures, 2 skipped) confirming zero cross-format regression.

13. Ran skills-first governance: resolve -> add-python-api (COMPOSE_EXISTING_SKILLS), manifest create --write (sfx-77954209ddb31b03, confirmed as the actually-persisted manifest via ls -t .local/skills-first/manifests/), hand-written receipt YAML, closeout --close -> CLOSE_OK.
